title: How Long Would You Last in an Antarctic Winter With No Shelter? #shorts
description_hook: You are dropped on the Antarctic plateau in the dead of winter, where the coldest months average -40 to -70 °C, with no tent and no shelter. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last in an Antarctic winter with no shelter? You're dropped on the plateau. The coldest months average -40 to -70 °C.
beats.img: a lone human silhouette seen from behind on a flat endless ice plateau under a dark polar night sky, faint green aurora overhead, blue snow glowing in moonlight

beats.say: Then the wind. About 17 mph, steady. The wind chill drops right off the weather service chart.
beats.img: fierce wind driving a low river of snow across rippled ice ridges at night, sastrugi carved sharp, a pale moon behind blowing ice crystals

beats.say: Any bare skin freezes in 5 minutes or less. Your face, your fingers. You stop feeling them.
beats.img: extreme close-up of a gloveless hand reaching into blowing polar snow, frost crystals forming on the knuckles, deep blue cold light

beats.say: Within hours, your core drops below 35 °C. That's hypothermia. Your thoughts slow down, and so does everything else.
beats.img: a dim glowing thermal-style outline of a human body curled up on the ice, its warm orange core fading into cold blue, endless dark plateau around it

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. Vostok once hit -89.2 °C. And sunrise is 6 months away.
